title: Netcompany's Guidewire practice puts it in competitor territory rather than complement territory
content:
Netcompany's insurance platform practice centres on Guidewire, which the research records as the dominant proprietary insurance core. That is enough to place the firm in competitor territory rather than complement territory: in an insurance engagement, the slot a record layer would occupy is already filled by a proprietary product the firm delivers.

The screen is about the software, not the firm. Netcompany is large and delivery-capable, and its Microsoft, AWS and Salesforce practices sit in the same column of the workbook. What disqualifies the insurance angle is which product sits at the centre of it, and no amount of delivery capacity changes that.

Recording the outcome keeps the qualification rule consistent across the corpus: leads whose central tool already owns the decision record rank below leads whose tooling moves work but keeps no record of what each step decided.
